orders_or_contracts.statement: Acquisition of 45,85,860 equity shares representing 100% of equity shareholding in M/S. Rajal Lefin & Commercial Private Limited (RLCPL) for total purchase consideration of Rs. 27,51,51,600 at Rs. 60 per equity share.

Issuance and allotment of up to 27,51,51,600 fully paid-up equity shares of face value Re. 1 each at Re. 1 per share to shareholders of RLCPL by way of share swap, discharging entire purchase consideration.

Acquisition of 100% Shareholding in M/s Rajal Lefin & Commercial Private Limited (RLCPL): The Company proposes to acquire 45,85,860 equity shares of RLCPL, representing 100% of its equity shareholding. The total purchase consideration for this acquisition is Rs. 27,51,51,600/- at a price of Rs. 60/- per equity share. In consideration, the Company intends to issue and allot up to 27,51,51,600 fully paid-up equity shares of the Company, having a face value of Re. 1/- each at a price of Re. 1/- per equity share, to the shareholders of RLCPL by way of share swap.

outlook.statement: The sector is still not encouraging and also the company is looking for better opportunities and growth in the field of finance and investment.
Expansion of existing activities: enhancing focus on loan against shares and securities, loan against properties and corporate loan and working capital loan.
Differentiated Services: providing all diversified service portfolio under one umbrella to cater most of the customer needs and demands.
Brand recognition: making necessary arrangements for brand reorganization.

risks: The Company has laid down a well-defined Risk Management Policy covering the risk mapping, trend analysis, risk exposure, potential impact and risk mitigation process. A detailed exercise is being carried out to identify, evaluate, manage and monitor both business and non-business risks.
Economic Downturn: If the economic downturn is prolonged it can reduce the financing need of people due to shrinking business opportunities.
Private Banks: Private Banks are also working on the similar business model as the NBFCs do, thereby giving a very strong competition to the NBFC's.
RBI and Government restrictions: With more stringent norms governing the functioning of NBFC and certain government restrictions act as a hindrance in smooth functioning of NBFC.
No commodity price risk or foreign exchange risk and hedging activities to report during the financial year under review.
Inherent limitations of internal financial controls over financial reporting, including possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls
Projections of internal financial controls evaluation to future periods subject to risk that controls may become inadequate due to changes in conditions or deterioration in compliance
